name: Chalcolithic Period
shortDesc: Copper Age; early settled agriculture and first urbanization in Mesopotamia and Levant

events.description: Ubaid culture flourishes in Mesopotamia
events.significance: Proto-urban settlements emerge along rivers

events.description: First cities rise at Uruk and Eridu
events.significance: Beginning of urban civilization

events.description: Earliest pictographic writing (proto-cuneiform) at Uruk
events.significance: Humanity's first written records

worldEvents.description: Cucuteni-Trypillia culture builds mega-sites in Ukraine with up to 15,000 inhabitants — the world's largest Neolithic settlements
Early farming settlements emerge at Mehrgarh in modern Pakistan, ancestors of the later Indus Valley Civilization
Caral civilization begins in coastal Peru — the oldest known civilization in the Americas
Yangshao culture develops sophisticated painted pottery and millet farming along the Yellow River

primarySources.name: Proto-Cuneiform Tablet from Uruk
primarySources.description: Among the oldest written records in history, these clay tablets from Uruk use pictographic symbols to track grain and livestock. The world's first writing was invented for accounting.

name: Early Bronze Age
shortDesc: First cities; cuneiform writing; Sumerian city-states; Old Kingdom Egypt; pyramids
biblicalContext: Primordial narratives; Table of Nations; Tower of Babel

events.description: Egypt unified under Narmer/Menes
events.significance: First Egyptian dynasty; start of pharaonic civilization

events.description: Great Pyramid of Giza completed
events.significance: Pinnacle of Old Kingdom engineering

events.description: Sargon of Akkad creates first empire
events.significance: First recorded multi-city empire in history

events.description: Third Dynasty of Ur (Ur III) rises
events.significance: Sumerian renaissance; elaborate temple-ziggurats built

worldEvents.description: Stonehenge constructed in stages on Salisbury Plain — megalithic monument aligned with the summer solstice
Indus Valley Civilization peaks at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro: planned cities with sewage systems, standardized weights, and a population of 50,000
Longshan culture develops walled towns, fine black pottery, and early bronze; traditions of the legendary Xia dynasty begin
Norte Chico/Caral civilization in Peru builds monumental pyramids and irrigation canals — the oldest known city complex in the Western Hemisphere

primarySources.name: Pyramid Texts (Pyramid of Unas)
primarySources.description: The oldest known religious texts in the world, carved on the walls of Pharaoh Unas's pyramid at Saqqara. They contain 228 spells to ensure the pharaoh's safe passage to the afterlife and his transformation into a star.

primarySources.name: Epic of Gilgamesh (early version)
primarySources.description: The world's oldest epic poem, from Sumerian Ur. It tells of King Gilgamesh's quest for immortality, his friendship with the wild man Enkidu, and a great flood survived by one righteous man — a story that predates and parallels the Noah narrative.

name: Middle Bronze Age
shortDesc: Amorite kingdoms; Old Babylonian Empire; Hyksos in Egypt; Canaanite city-state system
biblicalContext: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph — the Patriarchal period

events.description: Hammurabi becomes king of Babylon
events.significance: Law code promulgated; first written legal system

events.description: Proto-Sinaitic alphabet invented in Sinai/Canaan
events.significance: Ancestor of Hebrew, Greek, and all modern alphabets

events.description: Hyksos seize control of northern Egypt
events.significance: First foreign rulers of Egypt; introduced chariots and bronze weapons

worldEvents.description: Minoan civilization reaches its height on Crete — the palace of Knossos is built, Linear A script developed, and Minoan merchants trade across the Mediterranean
Shang Dynasty rises along the Yellow River; oracle bone divination and early Chinese writing emerge
Indus Valley Civilization collapses; Vedic culture and the Sanskrit language begin to emerge in the Punjab
Olmec civilization begins on Mexico's Gulf Coast — the 'mother culture' of Mesoamerica, developing early calendars and colossal stone heads

primarySources.name: Code of Hammurabi
primarySources.description: A black diorite stele inscribed with 282 laws covering contracts, property, family, and criminal justice. The prologue promises to establish justice so 'the strong may not oppress the weak.' The laws include famous principles of proportional justice.
primarySources.excerpt: If a man destroys the eye of another man, they shall destroy his eye. If he breaks another man's bone, they shall break his bone.

primarySources.name: Egyptian Execration Texts
primarySources.description: Ritual texts inscribed on clay figurines or pottery, listing the names of Egypt's enemies — including the rulers of Canaanite cities like Shechem, Jerusalem, and Ashkelon. These are the earliest Egyptian references to biblical cities.

name: Late Bronze Age
shortDesc: Egyptian New Kingdom; Hittite Empire; Amarna international system; widespread trade networks

events.description: Battle of Megiddo — Thutmose III defeats Canaanite coalition
events.significance: Egypt establishes dominance over Canaan

events.description: Akhenaten's religious revolution; worship of Aten
events.significance: First documented monotheistic state religion

events.description: Battle of Kadesh — Egypt vs. Hittites
events.significance: Oldest known peace treaty; Ramesses II and Hattusili III

events.description: Bronze Age Collapse — widespread destruction across the eastern Mediterranean
events.significance: Collapse of major palace economies; Ugarit, Hatti, and Mycenae destroyed

worldEvents.description: Mycenaean Greece flourishes — the era of the Trojan War cycle immortalized by Homer. Mycenae, Tiryns, and Athens build massive palace complexes
Minoan civilization collapses suddenly around 1450 BCE, possibly from the eruption of Thera (Santorini) and Mycenaean invasion
Shang Dynasty at its peak — sophisticated bronze ritual vessels, oracle bone divination, and ancestor worship become central to Chinese culture
The Rigveda composed — the oldest scriptures of Hinduism, containing hymns to Agni, Indra, and Varuna still recited today

primarySources.name: Amarna Letters
primarySources.description: Clay tablets discovered at Akhenaten's capital containing diplomatic letters between the Egyptian pharaoh and Canaanite city-kings. Letters mention Megiddo, Lachish, Jerusalem, Gezer, and Shechem — cities of the Torah — by name.
primarySources.excerpt: Say to the king, my lord, my Sun, my god: I am the dirt at the feet of the king, my lord, my Sun, my god. I have prostrated myself seven times and seven times. — King of Jerusalem (EA 287)

primarySources.name: Merneptah Stele
primarySources.description: A victory inscription by Pharaoh Merneptah celebrating his campaigns in Canaan. Contains the earliest known mention of 'Israel' outside the Bible — the only ancient Egyptian text to name Israel as a people.
primarySources.excerpt: Canaan is plundered with every hardship. Ashkelon is taken; Gezer is captured; Yano'am is made non-existent. Israel is laid waste and his seed is no more.

name: Iron Age I
shortDesc: Bronze Age Collapse; Philistine settlement; early Israelite tribal confederacy; Sea Peoples
biblicalContext: Settlement of Canaan; period of the Judges; early monarchy

events.description: Fall of Ugarit; Sea Peoples invade Egypt and Canaan
events.significance: Final blow to Bronze Age palace system

events.description: Philistines capture the Ark of the Covenant at Aphek
events.significance: Crisis that leads to demand for Israelite kingship

events.description: David becomes king of all Israel at Hebron
events.significance: United Monarchy established; Jerusalem conquered

worldEvents.description: Phoenicians develop the first true alphabet — 22 consonants adopted from proto-Sinaitic script, ancestor of Hebrew, Greek, Latin, and ultimately every modern alphabet
Greek Dark Ages: palace culture collapses, population plummets, writing is lost for 400 years. Small farming villages replace the great Mycenaean citadels
Zhou Dynasty overthrows the Shang and establishes a feudal system across China. 'The Mandate of Heaven' becomes the legitimizing principle for rule
Olmec civilization at San Lorenzo reaches its peak, carving colossal stone heads and developing the earliest Mesoamerican calendar systems

primarySources.name: Gezer Calendar
primarySources.description: A small limestone tablet found at biblical Gezer inscribed with an agricultural poem listing seasonal activities — harvest, planting, pruning. One of the oldest known Hebrew inscriptions, written in early Phoenician-Hebrew script.
primarySources.excerpt: Two months of harvest. Two months of planting. Two months of late planting. A month of hoeing flax. A month of barley-harvest...

primarySources.name: Mesha Stele (Moabite Stone)
primarySources.description: A black basalt stele from Dibon in Jordan, inscribed by Mesha, King of Moab, describing his revolt against Israel. It mentions the tribe of Gad, the Israelite king Omri by name, and possibly contains the oldest extrabiblical reference to 'the House of David.'
primarySources.excerpt: I am Mesha, son of Chemosh...king of Moab...And Omri, king of Israel, he afflicted Moab many days...

name: Iron Age II
shortDesc: United and Divided Monarchy; Assyrian Empire domination; Neo-Babylonian rise
biblicalContext: Kings of Israel and Judah; major prophets; Assyrian exile

events.description: Kingdom splits into Israel (north) and Judah (south) after Solomon's death
events.significance: Permanent division; two separate biblical kingdoms

events.description: Assyria conquers Samaria; Northern Kingdom of Israel destroyed
events.significance: Ten tribes exiled; 'Lost Tribes of Israel'

events.description: Sennacherib besieges Jerusalem; miraculous deliverance
events.significance: Isaiah's prophecy fulfilled; Hezekiah's tunnel built

worldEvents.description: Homer composes the Iliad and Odyssey (c. 800 BCE), defining works of Western literature. Greek city-states rise; the Olympic Games begin in 776 BCE
Rome founded (753 BCE, traditional date). Etruscan civilization flourishes in northern Italy with advanced metalwork and religious practices
Carthage founded by Phoenician settlers (c. 814 BCE). It grows into a Mediterranean commercial empire controlling trade routes across North Africa and Spain
The major Upanishads are composed (800–500 BCE), developing concepts of Atman and Brahman. Mahavira founds Jainism; the Buddha is born in Nepal (c. 563 BCE)

primarySources.name: Siloam Inscription
primarySources.description: Carved into the wall of Hezekiah's tunnel in Jerusalem, this inscription records the dramatic moment when two teams tunneling from opposite ends heard each other and broke through. It matches 2 Kings 20:20 precisely.
primarySources.excerpt: ...And this is the account of the breakthrough: While the workers were still lifting the pick, each toward his fellow...there was heard the voice of a man calling his fellow, for there was a crack in the rock on the right side...

primarySources.name: Lachish Letters
primarySources.description: Ink-on-pottery letters (ostraca) exchanged between officers at Lachish as the Babylonian army advanced. They describe failing military signals and the chaos of the final days of Judah — and match Jeremiah 34:7 almost word for word.
primarySources.excerpt: Let my lord know that we are watching for the fire signals of Lachish according to all the signs which my lord has given, for we cannot see Azekah.

name: Babylonian–Persian Period
shortDesc: Babylonian exile; Cyrus Edict (538 BCE); Return to Zion; Second Temple foundation

events.description: Nebuchadnezzar destroys Jerusalem and the First Temple
events.significance: Babylonian exile begins; major theological crisis for Israel

events.description: Cyrus the Great captures Babylon without battle
events.significance: Persian Empire replaces Neo-Babylonian Empire

events.description: Cyrus Edict — Jews permitted to return to Judah
events.significance: End of exile; Isaiah 45 prophecy fulfilled

events.description: Second Temple dedicated in Jerusalem
events.significance: Restoration of Temple worship after 70-year gap

worldEvents.description: Golden Age of Athens: the Parthenon is built (447–432 BCE), Socrates teaches in the agora, and Aeschylus, Sophocles, and Euripides write. Democracy is born.
Confucius (551–479 BCE) teaches ethics, governance, and social harmony. Sun Tzu writes The Art of War. This is China's Axial Age.
The Buddha attains enlightenment at Bodh Gaya (c. 528 BCE) and teaches the Dharma. Buddhism spreads across South Asia within a generation.
Zoroastrianism becomes the official Persian religion under the Achaemenid kings — its ideas of one God, good vs. evil, resurrection, and judgment profoundly influenced post-exilic Judaism

primarySources.name: Cyrus Cylinder
primarySources.description: A clay cylinder from Babylon on which Cyrus the Great declares that he has conquered Babylon peacefully and will allow all deported peoples to return home and rebuild their temples. The decree directly parallels Ezra 1:2–4.
primarySources.excerpt: I gathered all their inhabitants and restored to them their dwellings. And the gods of Sumer and Akkad whom Nabonidus had brought into Babylon...I returned them to their places.

primarySources.name: Tel Dan Inscription
primarySources.description: Basalt fragments from Tel Dan in northern Israel bearing the Aramaic phrase 'House of David' — the first extrabiblical confirmation of the Davidic dynasty. The inscription was made by a Syrian king celebrating his victories over Israel and Judah.
primarySources.excerpt: ...I killed [Jehoram son of] Ahab king of Israel, and I killed [Ahaziah son of Jehoram kin]g of the House of David...
